brief.headline: Push for faster payment in exchange for a 2–3% price cut — we're 1.36% of their revenue and they carry heavy debt

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 2–3% price reduction if we move to 15-day or pay-on-receipt terms
priceAsk.basis: Our price sits in the market-fair band (₹60–81/kg, typical ₹66–73/kg). They owe 2.25x their own cash, so faster payment has real value to them — worth trading for a small cut that still keeps them profitable.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (or on receipt) in return for the price cut above
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15-day terms frees up ₹61.76 L of our cash; paying immediately frees ₹1.24 Cr — but only do it if the price cut justifies locking that cash

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji keeps only 2.3% profit on each sale, so there's little room for a big price cut without hurting them. But they owe 2.25x their own cash (₹238.85 Cr total debt) and we're 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue — a meaningful customer. Their health score is D (21/100), so they need our business and will value faster payment. Push the payment-for-price swap, not a hard squeeze on price alone.

evidence.point: We're a significant customer to them
evidence.figure: Our ₹15.03 Cr spend is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They carry heavy debt relative to their own money
evidence.figure: Debt is 2.25x their equity; total owed ₹238.85 Cr

evidence.point: Our current price is market-fair, slightly favourable to us
evidence.figure: ₹66.48/KG sits in ask band ₹60–81/kg, typical ₹66–73/kg — verdict: MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: India export reference price is lower
evidence.figure: Export unit value 42.95 ₹/kg — but that's bulk commodity, not pharma-grade IP material
Health score D (21/100); return on capital 8.2%

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker (₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B 62/100) — established dextrose supplier, much stronger financially, a solid second source

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller (₹365.39 Cr revenue) making Dextrose ANHYDROUS IV-fluid grade — exact form match; confirm IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C 53/100) — growing capacity in starch and dextrose

risks: Sayaji's health is weak (D 21/100) and debt high (2.25x) — pushing too hard on price could squeeze their thin 2.3% margin and risk supply stability; lead with the payment-for-price trade instead
We already pay ₹66.48/KG, which is the best price we have and sits in the fair market band — there's limited room to push price alone without a quid pro quo
They make only 2.3% profit, so any price cut comes almost entirely from their margin — keep the ask modest (2–3%) and tie it to a benefit for them (faster cash)
If they can't move on price or terms, qualify Gulshan Polyols or Sanstar as a backup now — don't wait until supply is at risk
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to keep Sayaji as our Dextrose supplier — and we're ready to help your cash flow by moving to 15-day payment if you can meet us with a small price improvement that reflects the faster cash.
